question: What is a gene?
options: The complete set of DNA in an organism
A section of DNA that codes for a specific protein
A type of chromosome found in gametes
A mutation in the DNA sequence
correct: A section of DNA that codes for a specific protein

question: What does homozygous mean?
options: Having two different alleles for a gene
Having one dominant and one recessive allele
Having two identical alleles for a gene
Having no alleles for a gene
correct: Having two identical alleles for a gene

question: A dominant allele is represented by B and recessive by b. Which genotype would show the recessive phenotype?
options: BB
Bb
bB
bb

question: What type of cell division produces gametes?
options: Mitosis
Binary fission
Meiosis
Budding

question: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a recessive allele. Two carrier parents (Ff × Ff) have a child. What is the probability the child has cystic fibrosis?
Which statement about polydactyly is correct?
options: It is caused by a recessive allele and causes thick mucus in the lungs
It is caused by a dominant allele and results in extra fingers or toes
It is caused by a recessive allele and results in extra fingers or toes
It is caused by a dominant allele and causes thick mucus in the lungs
correct: It is caused by a dominant allele and results in extra fingers or toes

question: What sex chromosomes does a human male have?
options: XX
XY
YY
X only

question: Which of the following is an example of continuous variation?
options: Blood group
Tongue rolling
Height
Attached or free earlobes

question: What is natural selection?
options: Humans selecting organisms with desirable traits to breed
The process by which better adapted individuals survive and pass on their genes
A random change in the DNA sequence
The formation of new species through isolation
correct: The process by which better adapted individuals survive and pass on their genes

question: Who proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection?
options: Gregor Mendel
Louis Pasteur
Charles Darwin
Alexander Fleming

question: What is selective breeding?
options: Inserting a gene from one organism into another
Humans choosing organisms with desired traits and breeding them together
The natural process of evolution over millions of years
A type of mutation that improves an organism's characteristics
correct: Humans choosing organisms with desired traits and breeding them together

question: How is human insulin now produced commercially?
options: By extracting it from pigs and cows
By inserting the human insulin gene into bacteria
By synthesising it entirely from chemicals
By selective breeding of insulin-producing animals
correct: By inserting the human insulin gene into bacteria

question: What do fossils provide evidence for?
options: How organisms are classified into kingdoms
How species have changed over millions of years
The exact DNA sequence of extinct organisms
How genetic engineering works
correct: How species have changed over millions of years

question: What is a mutation?
options: The passing of alleles from parent to offspring
A random change in the DNA sequence
The fusion of two gametes at fertilisation
The separation of chromosomes during meiosis
correct: A random change in the DNA sequence

question: What does the binomial nomenclature system give each organism?
options: A common name in English
A two-part Latin name consisting of genus and species
A number based on its position in the food chain
A classification into one of five kingdoms
correct: A two-part Latin name consisting of genus and species

question: State what is meant by the term genome.
mark_scheme: The complete set of genetic information / DNA of an organism (1).

question: State the difference between genotype and phenotype.
mark_scheme: Genotype is the alleles an organism carries (1); phenotype is the observable characteristics resulting from the genotype (1) — accept either for 1 mark.

question: State the sex chromosomes found in a human female.
Name the scientist who proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection.
Explain why meiosis is important for sexual reproduction.
mark_scheme: Meiosis produces haploid gametes (1); containing half the normal number of chromosomes (1); so when two gametes fuse at fertilisation the full chromosome number is restored (1); produces genetic variation in offspring (1) — any two.

question: Explain how a mutation can lead to a new phenotype.
mark_scheme: A mutation is a random change in the DNA sequence (1); changes the sequence of bases (1); may alter the protein produced (1); this can result in a new or altered characteristic (1) — any two.

question: Describe how selective breeding is carried out.
mark_scheme: Identify individuals with the desired characteristic (1); breed these individuals together (1); select offspring with the desired characteristic (1); repeat over many generations (1) — any two.

question: Explain how antibiotic resistance in bacteria is an example of natural selection.
mark_scheme: Random mutation produces some resistant bacteria (1); antibiotics kill non-resistant bacteria (1); resistant bacteria survive and reproduce (1); resistance genes passed to offspring (1) — any two.

question: Two parents are both carriers of cystic fibrosis (Ff). Explain the possible outcomes for their children.
mark_scheme: FF — unaffected and not a carrier (1); Ff — carrier but unaffected (1); ff — has cystic fibrosis (1); 25% chance of having the condition (1) — any two.

question: Explain the process of natural selection using an example.
mark_scheme: Variation exists within a population (1); some individuals have characteristics better suited to the environment (1); these individuals are more likely to survive and reproduce (1); they pass advantageous alleles to offspring (1); over many generations the advantageous characteristic becomes more common (1) — any three.

question: Describe how genetic engineering is used to produce human insulin.
mark_scheme: The gene for human insulin is identified and cut out (1); using enzymes (1); the gene is inserted into a bacterial plasmid (1); the bacteria reproduce and produce human insulin (1); insulin is harvested and purified (1) — any three.

question: Explain how sex is determined in humans.
mark_scheme: Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes (1); one pair are sex chromosomes (1); females are XX, males are XY (1); sperm carry either X or Y chromosome (1); eggs always carry X chromosome (1); if Y sperm fertilises egg — male; if X sperm — female (1) — any three.

question: Explain how Darwin's theory of evolution by natural selection works, and why it was not immediately accepted.
mark_scheme: Variation exists in a population (1); individuals better adapted survive and reproduce (1); advantageous alleles passed to offspring (1); over many generations species change (1). Not accepted because: lack of fossil evidence at the time (1); conflicted with religious beliefs (1); mechanism of inheritance not understood (1) — any four.

question: Tall plants (T) are dominant over dwarf plants (t). Two heterozygous tall plants are crossed. Use a Punnett square to explain the expected ratio of tall to dwarf plants in the offspring.
mark_scheme: Both parents are Tt (1); Punnett square gives TT, Tt, Tt, tt (1); 3 tall : 1 dwarf ratio (1); TT and Tt show tall phenotype (1); only tt shows dwarf phenotype (1) — any four.

question: Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of selective breeding.
mark_scheme: Advantages: produces organisms with desired characteristics (1); can increase food production / disease resistance (1); has been practised successfully for thousands of years (1). Disadvantages: reduces genetic variation — inbreeding (1); may make populations vulnerable to new diseases (1); can cause health problems in animals e.g. hip problems in dogs (1) — any four.

question: Explain what fossils are and describe three types of evidence they provide for evolution.
mark_scheme: Fossils are preserved remains of ancient organisms (1); found in rock layers (1); show that organisms have changed over time (1); show common ancestors between species (1); gaps in fossil record show extinction events (1); older fossils in deeper rock layers (1) — any four.

question: Explain how cystic fibrosis is inherited. In your answer, use a genetic cross to show the possible outcomes when two carrier parents have children.
mark_scheme: Cystic fibrosis caused by recessive allele (1); carriers are heterozygous Ff (1); Punnett square: FF, Ff, Ff, ff (1); 25% chance of having cystic fibrosis (ff) (1); 50% chance of being a carrier (Ff) (1); 25% chance of being unaffected non-carrier (FF) (1) — any five.

question: Evaluate the use of genetic engineering in medicine and agriculture. Include both advantages and disadvantages in your answer.
mark_scheme: Advantages: produces human insulin for diabetics (1); can produce disease-resistant crops (1); faster than selective breeding (1); can introduce entirely new characteristics (1). Disadvantages: ethical concerns about 'playing God' (1); GM crops may affect ecosystems (1); long-term effects unknown (1); patented seeds may be expensive for farmers (1); risk of genes spreading to wild plants (1) — any six.

question: Explain how speciation occurs when populations become geographically isolated. Include the roles of variation, natural selection and mutation in your answer.
mark_scheme: A population becomes geographically isolated (1); no interbreeding between groups (1); variation exists within each group (1); different environmental pressures cause different natural selection (1); mutations occur randomly in each group (1); different alleles become more common in each group (1); over time the groups become so different they can no longer interbreed (1); a new species has formed (1) — any six.
